newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Jan 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Jan 20.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Local Nissan assembler Automakers minority shareholders are to be paid up to 247 million rand in a scheme to delist the company ahead of bringing in an international group as the controlling shareholder.

- It would not be surprising if many Taiwan-funded firms -- especially money-losing textile companies -- closed their operations in South Africa soon a deputy director of Taiwan's economics ministry said on Sunday.

- The South African revenue service is to acquire a new computer system that will allow it to access the records of commercial banks' interest payments to clients, check the accuracy of tax returns and catch more tax evaders, says inland revenue commissioner Trevor van Heerden.

- Most of the South African Revenue Services's (SARS) estimated 11,000 employees have received an interim incentive bonus payment worth a total of about 75 million rand for exceeding revenue and arrear tax collection targets, Piet Liebenberg, the chief executive officer of SARS, said last week.

- The spate of health and safety reports against SD Warren, the U.S.-based Sappi subsidiary, by the United Paperworkers International Union was "engineered" to resist a new labour contract aimed at improving productivity, Eugene van As, Sappi chairman, said last week.
- Roy Andersen, the outgoing Johannesburg Stock Exchange president, retires from the exchange at the end of this month to join insurer Liberty Life as heir apparent to Donny Gordon, its chairman.

- The top management of Compass Insurance, the short-term insurer, has resigned because of diffrences over management style with a new board appointed last month, Joseph Daly, the former managing director of Compass, said at the weekend.
- On the eve of the cabinet decision on whether or not to sell arms to Syria, Deputy President Thabo Mbeki took a defiant stand against the United States government's criticism of the proposed deal.
- Former Free State premier Terror Lekota is receiving wide support among provincial ANC branches.
- Taiwanese Foreign Minister John Chang said on Sunday that patience would be needed in shaping a new relationship with South Africa, which is breaking off diplomatic ties in favour of Beijing.
- An executive member of the South African Football Association, Derek Blanckensee, has resigned.
